ecb-2026-09.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which sets policy rates for the euro area at scheduled meetings through the year. Its decisions set the cost of credit across the currency bloc and transmit to bond yields, bank lending and the euro itself.
ecb-2026-09.recent: The decision lands into a run of central banks holding rather than moving: the RBA held its rate steady as the housing market softened, while a hike remains possible. The dollar has fallen to its lowest level since May with a rate hike in doubt, and inflation prints elsewhere are drifting up, with India's retail rate rising to 4.45% in July from 4.38% in June.

fomc-2026-09.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the target range for overnight bank lending. Its decisions set the cost of borrowing across the dollar economy and reprice every asset quoted against the dollar.

boe-2026-09.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its decisions set the cost of borrowing across the UK economy, feeding into mortgage rates, gilt yields and sterling.
boe-2026-09.recent: The Bank of England has been expanding a digital pound pilot with Polygon, testing settlement alongside stablecoins — work that sits beside the rate-setting question rather than inside it. On the rates side, the meeting follows the RBA's decision to hold steady as its housing market softens, and a dollar that has fallen to its lowest level since May.

boj-2026-09.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which sets Japan's short-term interest rate at eight scheduled meetings a year. Its decisions move the yen, Japanese government bond yields, and the global carry trades funded in cheap Japanese money.
boj-2026-09.recent: The meeting follows a historic joint US-Japan intervention on 3 August that pushed the dollar to a one-month low, an unusual move by Washington against yen weakness. That same weakness nearly doubled Toyota's quarterly profit to $9.4 billion. The decision will settle how far the board goes to support the currency by policy rather than intervention.

uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly measure of UK consumer price inflation, covering the change in prices paid by households for a basket of goods and services. It anchors Bank of England rate policy, index-linked gilts and a range of benefit and pension upratings.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: The release lands as inflation prints elsewhere move markets: India's retail inflation rose to 4.45% in July from 4.38% in June, driven by food prices. This reading will settle where UK price growth sits against the Bank of England's target, and it feeds the uprating decisions that follow the September figure.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the target range for overnight bank lending. Its decisions move the cost of borrowing across the dollar economy and every asset priced against the dollar.
fomc-2026-10.recent: The committee meets while Trump renews his bid to fire Cook, reviving a fight over Fed independence. The dollar has fallen to its weakest since May, gold hit $4,392 an ounce, and traders are looking past CPI to the Fed's next tests. This decision settles the target range those positions are built against.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's governing council sets interest rates for the euro area, meeting on a fixed schedule through the year. Its decisions set the cost of credit across the currency bloc and transmit to bond yields and the euro's exchange rate.
ecb-2026-10.recent: The decision lands after a stretch in which other central banks have stayed put rather than moved: the RBA held its rate steady in August as the housing market softened, without ruling out another hike. Currency markets have already repriced, with the dollar falling to its lowest level since May as a rate hike came into doubt.

boj-2026-10.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board sets the short-term policy rate and decides the pace of its bond purchases at eight scheduled meetings a year. Its decisions drive the yen and the world's largest pool of low-cost carry-trade funding.
boj-2026-10.recent: This decision follows a historic joint US-Japan yen intervention on August 3, which pushed the dollar to a one-month low and marked Washington's move against Japanese yen weakness. The cheap yen has flattered exporters — Toyota's quarterly profit nearly doubled to $9.4 billion. At stake is whether the bank tightens to support the currency itself.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its decisions set the cost of borrowing across the sterling economy — mortgages, business credit and the pound's exchange rate.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the target range for overnight bank lending. Its decisions move borrowing costs across the dollar economy and every asset priced against the dollar.
fomc-2026-12.recent: The committee arrives at this meeting split, with a supply-shock regime complicating the read on inflation and a low-hire, low-fire labour market. The dollar has already fallen to its weakest since May with a rate hike in doubt, gold has run to $4,392 an ounce, and Trump's renewed move to fire Cook has reopened the fight over Fed independence.

fred-us-gdp-2026-08-26.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's quarterly estimate of US gross domestic product, released in successive vintages as more source data arrives. It is the broadest single measure of the world's largest economy, and sets the frame for rate expectations and the dollar.
fred-us-gdp-2026-08-26.recent: The release lands as growth readings elsewhere come in thin: Russia's economy ministry put annualized GDP gains at 0.6% in the first half, and Ukraine's budget deficit is running toward a record 35% of GDP in 2026. This estimate will settle how much momentum the US carried into the quarter.

fred-us-pce-2026-08-26.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's monthly report on personal consumption expenditures, which includes the PCE price index — the inflation gauge the Federal Reserve targets. It covers household spending and income, and sets the reference point for US rate policy.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of leaders of the world's twenty largest economies, rotating through a presidency that sets the agenda. It has no treaty power; its output is a communiqué that signals where the major economies intend to align on trade, finance and debt.
